question: Who is regarded as the ‘Mother of Indian Revolution’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madame Cama**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madame Cama** is widely regarded as the '**Mother of Indian Revolution**'.
 
• She was an important figure in the Indian independence movement and played a crucial role in advocating for India's freedom from British rule.
 
• Madame Cama was known for her fiery speeches and was deeply involved in the revolutionary activities against the British Empire.
 
• She also **unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag in 1907 **at the **International Socialist Conference in Stuttgart, Germany.**
 
• Her contributions to the freedom struggle were significant, and she inspired many young revolutionaries to join the cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madame Bhikaji Cama** was born on 24th September 1861 in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• She was a strong advocate for gender equality and worked tirelessly for the upliftment of women in society.
 
• Madame Cama was influenced by the social and political conditions of her time and was determined to fight against the injustices perpetrated by the British colonial rulers.
 
• She spent a significant part of her life in exile in Europe, where she continued her revolutionary activities and garnered international support for India's independence.
 
• Madame Cama passed away on 13th August 1936, but her legacy continues to inspire generations of Indians.
